thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#83421 — service=inference-runtime | rule=latency_p95 > 500ms for 2/5 intervals
kaela: Acked. I'm on it. paging to primary oncall.
kaela: looking at grafana: p95 spike to ~780ms across us-west-2, small number of hosts (~3/40) showing load.
sam: tagging in — just woke up, give me a minute to pull logs.
mohit: I see the same in traces: long tail on decoder step, correlate with KV cache misses.
kaela: running quick check: `kubectl top pod -n inference | grep runtime` — CPU a bit elevated on node g4-12-07.
priya: any customer impact reported? support dashboard shows 3 error-rate increases but looks like retries, no real 5xxs.
kaela: PD note said severity=page-low. No user-facing outage reported yet. looks transient.
incident-bot: ALERT: PD#83421 still unacknowledged for escalation window; escalated to sam (oncall-secondary).
sam: ack. I'm SSH'ing into the host to check process-level stats.
kaela: capture of the runtime logs from one host: ```
[2026-03-14T07:12:18Z] WARN kv_cache: miss for prefix abc123, fetching from s3, latency 320ms
[2026-03-14T07:12:19Z] WARN runtime: batch_size spike -> 12
[2026-03-14T07:12:20Z] INFO rpc: request queued 180ms
```
mohit: that pattern matches quick cold-key loads, happens after small scaleups or pre-warm misses. We had a small autoscaler bounce on that node ~07:10.
priya: hmm support mentions a chatty tenant running rerank jobs around that time. could be correlated.
sam: I can roll a targeted restart of the runtime on those hosts to clear local state and force KV warmup. anyone object?
kaela: go for it, do one at a time. add `--drain-wait 15s` flag.
sam: rolling now: host g4-12-07-3 restarted, observing CPU drop and latency returning toward norm.
incident-bot: PD#83421 auto-resolved by alerting system (alert condition cleared)
kaela: nice, looks like a ~4min blip total.
mohit: root cause candidate: short-lived KV cache missstorm due to autoscaler event + coincident heavy rerank workload. produces flapping alert signal.
priya: customer impact: minimal — retries absorbed and no 5xx; notify support to mark as "no impact" but flag tenant for noisy jobs.
kaela: quick follow-ups: 1) add a suppression window: require 3 consecutive intervals of p95>500ms before page, 2) add a KV-warmup short grace for autoscaler events, 3) add runbook snippet for targeted restart. anyone disagree?
sam: +1 on suppression. those alerts are a lot of noise and mask real incidents.
mohit: will prototype a short-lived heuristic: if autoscaler event detected in last 5m, apply 60s suppression for p95 pages. will open an infra ticket.
priya: I'll create a support playbook entry to watch tenant rerank spikes. Ticket: SUP-4872.
kaela: created infra ticket INFRA-2134 for alert tuning and runbook. assign to mohit for the heuristic and to sam for adding restart command to runbook.
incident-bot: Note: PD#83421 marked resolved and closed by alerting service.
riley: picking up next shift. thanks for the handoff — I'll check INFRA-2134 during my morning cycle and confirm suppression doesn't hide real regressions.
kaela: thanks all. no further action needed for customer-facing comms, triage tickets as above. I'll file a short blameless note in #postmortems if anything new shows up. :white_check_mark:
sam: leaving a quick command snippet for runbook: ```
# targeted restart, one host at a time
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=g4-12-07-3
sleep 45 # wait for warmup
```
kaela: closing thread. if it flaps again we'll escalate to rotation and consider rate-limiting the rerank tenant. :thumbsup:
